Intel, Oracle, IBM Join Objections to OKX-ICE Tokenized Stock Venue, Bringing Total to 26

The tech sector's resistance to tokenized stocks keeps building.

Intel, Oracle, IBM, and quantum computing firm IonQ are the latest companies to object to having their shares traded on OKXICE TSV, according to an updated public notice from the venue dated Monday.

Myriad: Which company will IPO next? Click to make your prediction.

The planned platform, a 50-50 joint venture between NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange and OKX's U.S. holding company, now lists 26 objecting issuers.

That's up from 22 in its Oct. 23 notice, which added Wells Fargo, Cisco, and Marvell. The tally stood at 16 on Oct. 19 and nine on Oct. 15, when the first batch included Verizon, Broadcom and UnitedHealth Group. In less than two weeks, the list has nearly tripled.

Technology companies dominate the roster. Microsoft, Alphabet, Broadcom, Qualcomm, Arm, Cisco, and now Intel and Oracle have all objected, along with banks Goldman Sachs and Wells Fargo.

IBM and IonQ add two quantum computing players. As before, the notices don't explain the companies' reasons or what an objection means for whether a stock can trade on the platform.

OKXICE TSV plans to let approved users trade tokenized U.S. stocks 24/7 through permissioned Uniswap v4 liquidity pools on OKX's XLayer blockchain, paired with stablecoins such as USDC.

Users must pass identity and sanctions checks and hold a nontransferable "soulbound" token to trade. The venue is set to operate under the SEC's innovation exemption, which the agency unveiled in September after the Clarity Act stalled in the Senate.

The latest notice highlights a key risk for investors. Each token represents a claim on a real share held by a third-party "tokenizer" through a registered broker-dealer. If that broker-dealer failed, the notice says, it's uncertain whether tokenized shares in a self-custodied wallet would count as customer property or be covered by the Securities Investor Protection Corporation, which protects brokerage customers when firms fail.

Wells Fargo, Cisco, Intuit Among 6 More Companies Objecting to Tokenized Stocks

The notice also says trades must be fully funded, with no margin or borrowing. Liquidity providers don't have to be registered market makers and can pull their liquidity at any time.

OKX and ICE first teamed up on tokenized securities earlier this year before unveiling plans for the venue this month.

Tech investors have turned to artificial intelligence (AI) stocks for investment returns. Over the last four years, they have probably been happy to see many of these stocks earn outsized gains.

What investors may have forgotten is that some of these are also dividend stocks. Admittedly, some pay negligible dividends, while others have required investors to sacrifice stock price growth for higher dividend returns.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Fortunately, a few pay a dividend well above the S&P 500 average of 1.1% without sacrificing growth. Thanks to AI, these three stocks offer the potential for such gains.

Image source: Getty Images.
IBM

International Business Machines (NYSE: IBM) has revived its tech business in recent years by pivoting more heavily into the cloud. The 2019 acquisition of Red Hat made it a leading cloud company, and, like other similar companies, it later embraced generative AI.

Its watsonx platform allows users to build, scale, and administer AI models, and it develops foundation models called Granite. Other offerings include agentic AI, cloud and quantum integration, and AI consulting services.

This technology helps support a yearly dividend of $6.76 per share. IBM has increased that payout for 31 straight years, and even with the AI-driven growth, it yields 2.7%. The increases are on track to continue, as it generated over $15 billion in free cash flow over the last year, well above the $6.3 billion it paid in dividends.

Admittedly, IBM is a slower-growing company, and its third-quarter revenue of $17 billion increased by only 5%. Moreover, even though the company has generally tracked the performance of the S&P 500 since CEO Arvind Krishna took over in 2020, it is down over the past year.

However, with a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 21, the stock sells at an attractive valuation. With the stock and the dividend likely to continue rising, these conditions should continue to make IBM stock a buy.

Digital Realty Trust

Digital Realty Trust (NYSE: DLR) is a real estate investment trust (REIT) operating data centers. Although this is technically a real estate stock, it has capitalized on the data center construction boom. The REIT is in a strong position, as insatiable industry demand provides it with a large customer base.

Demand is such that Digital Realty suspended payout hikes in 2022, probably to devote more capital to expansion. Still, at an annual dividend of $4.88 per share, it offers a dividend yield of 2.9%. Moreover, considering its $8.27 per share in diluted funds from operations (FFO) income over the trailing 12 months, it can likely afford its payout.

Over the five years to October 26, 2026, one software stock beat 123 of its 126 industry peers. The standout is JFrog (FROG), an application software company that sells the JFrog Platform as a system of record for the software its customers build. A run like that can come from a strong industry or from the company alone. Take a guess: was it JFrog's industry, or JFrog itself?

How Far JFrog Is Ahead Of Its Industry

JFrog stock rose 193.2% over those five years, while the typical company in the Application Software industry (the median one, of any size) lost 47.1%. Here is how JFrog sits beside its sector, the typical stock and the S&P 500:

JFrog's shareholders made money in an industry where most companies' shares fell. Among the larger companies in its industry, only Palantir Technologies rose more.

Was It JFrog's Industry?

No. JFrog rose against its industry's tide. The S&P 500 climbed 67.8% over the five years, even as the typical stock fell 3.8%. JFrog still rose far more than the index.

The closer the comparison gets to JFrog's own business, the worse its neighbors did. The typical Information Technology company fell 21.9%. Application Software ranked last of the sector's 12 industries on that measure. JFrog had no tailwind from its industry, and the gain was the company's own.

What Did JFrog's Business Do?

JFrog grew its sales much faster than its industry. Its revenue grew 24.3% a year on average over the past three years, compared with 11.1% for the typical application software company.

In the four quarters to June 2026, JFrog's revenue was 242.2% higher than in the four quarters to June 2021. Its reported operating loss narrowed over the same years to 11.1% of revenue from 21.8%. The company still reported a loss per share in both years, leaving it with no price-to-earnings multiple worth quoting. On the prior four quarters of sales, investors paid 17.9 times at the end of September 2021 and 19.7 times at the end of September 2026. A 30.1% increase in JFrog's diluted share count also held back the gain for each share. The stock's lead came mostly from selling far more, and only partly from investors paying about 10% more for each dollar of sales.

Shares of International Business Machines (IBM) rose 0.26% on October 22, 2026, during the session following its fiscal Q3 2026 report, while the S&P 500 fell 1.2%. Microsoft, Amazon and Oracle each fell more than 2% that day. Revenue came in just 0.7% above analysts' estimates and earnings per share topped expectations by 2.2%. With a beat this small, the more telling changes sit further down the report.
So where did IBM's quarter actually turn?

IBM's Software Business Sped Back Up

The turn came in software, which generated 44.4% of IBM's revenue in fiscal 2025, more than any other segment. Management said software revenue growth jumped four points from the second quarter to reach 9%. It also said the division led a broader pickup across IBM's segments, with infrastructure growth rising to 5%.

Management said the biggest difference came from a single part of the software business. On the October 21 call, executives explained that transactional sales, the software IBM sells in individual deals rather than as recurring revenue, make up about 20% of the software book. These sales fell by double digits in the second quarter, taking 4 to 5 points off software growth. In the third quarter, they rose by double digits. This swing was larger than software's four-point pickup. Management also said its automation business faced a tougher comparison.

How Much Of IBM's Software Jump Was Catch-Up?

Management said about a quarter of the jump came from large deals that slipped out of the second quarter and closed in the third. The other three-quarters was new business. For transaction processing, its mainframe software, management said the deferred second-quarter deals landed on top of a normal third-quarter mainframe buying cycle.

For IBM as a whole, the quarter looks more like a recovery from the second quarter than a step up. Total reported revenue grew 4.7% from a year earlier, an improvement from 1.1% in the second quarter. That pace still trails the first quarter, when revenue grew 9.5%.

What Does IBM Now Expect For 2026?

Management held its forecast for 2026 revenue growth at 4% to 5% at constant currency, the same range it gave in July. The company also raised its forecast for the year's increase in free cash flow to more than $1 billion. For the software division, management now expects full-year growth of about 7% to 8%.

Management also expects part of the quarter's strength to fade. Transaction processing, IBM's mainframe software, grew 10% in the quarter. Executives do not expect that double-digit pace to continue, noting that growth might moderate from the third quarter into the fourth. While Red Hat bookings grew in the high teens, and management said such bookings growth turns into good revenue growth, the company did not want to comment on 2027 growth. It said it would quantify its view in January.

Quantum Corporation QMCO delivered positive operating cash flow in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 despite persistent supply chain challenges. However, continued shortages of tape drives and certain disk drives remain a key hurdle, limiting the company's ability to fully capitalize on strong customer demand. While management expects supply conditions to improve over the year, component availability and pricing pressures could influence its ability to sustain cash flow generation.

Quantum generated approximately $0.9 million in operating cash flow during the quarter, with capital expenditures totaling $0.4 million, representing less than 0.5% of revenues. Revenues increased 25.7% year over year and approximately 4% sequentially to $80.8 million, exceeding management's guidance. GAAP gross margin improved 360 basis points (bps) sequentially to 39.3%, supported by stronger pricing, disciplined cost management and favorable inventory performance. Adjusted EBITDA was $8 million compared with $1 million in the preceding quarter.

The company's strengthened financial position offers additional support. Quantum ended the quarter with $54.6 million in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash, up from $16.2 million at fiscal 2026-end. Following its private placement and debt repayments, outstanding debt declined to zero from $144.8 million at March-end. Management expects minimal interest expenses going forward, potentially easing pressure on cash generation.

However, supply constraints continue to restrict revenue conversion despite growing backlog and strong bookings. On the last earnings call, management highlighted that tape drive availability remained inadequate through August, with no meaningful improvement observed. Although increased production is anticipated later in the year, near-term revenue upside depends heavily on Quantum's ability to fulfill customer orders.

For the second quarter of fiscal 2027, Quantum projects revenues of $82 million, plus or minus $2 million, and adjusted EBITDA of $6 million, plus or minus $1 million. Management also expects year-over-year gross margin improvement despite component-related pricing volatility. Maintaining operating expense discipline and generating consistent positive cash flow remain key priorities. Quantum's improved liquidity, profitability and debt-free balance sheet provide support, although sustained cash flow performance will depend partly on easing supply shortages.

Taking a Look at QMCO's Competitors

International Business Machines' IBM cash generation continues to support investment requirements and shareholder distributions. In the first nine months of 2026, free cash flow increased approximately $600 million year over year to $7.8 billion, representing 8% growth. Adjusted EBITDA rose approximately $1 billion over the same period, supporting cash generation despite higher capital expenditure, cash taxes and net interest expenses. Third-quarter operating pretax margin expanded 70 bps, while Software and Infrastructure segment profit margins increased 210 bps and 120 bps, respectively. IBM returned $4.8 billion to shareholders through dividends during the first nine months. Management now expects full-year free cash flow growth of more than $1 billion, above its previous expectation of approximately $1 billion. Productivity initiatives and recurring software revenue underpin IBM's ability to fund strategic investments, service acquisition-related obligations and sustain capital returns.

title: Oracle, IBM and Intel Have Opted Out of OKX-ICE Stock Tokens, Venue’s Own Notice Shows
detail:
Oracle, IBM and Intel Have Opted Out of OKX-ICE Stock Tokens, Venue’s Own Notice Shows
OKXICE stock token objections reach 26 · Unchained
Unchained
Tue, October 27, 2026 at 3:00 AM MST 3 min read
ORCL
IBM
INTC
MRNA
CSCO
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The tokenized stock venue run by Intercontinental Exchange and OKX now counts 26 companies that have objected to tokenized versions of their shares trading on it, according to a revised public notice the venue published dated Oct. 26. That is four more than the 22 objectors Unchained reported on Oct. 23.

The last four names on the notice's list are IBM, IonQ, Oracle and Intel. Moderna, Cisco and Marvell Technology also appear. None of those seven were named in Unchained's earlier coverage. The full list also includes Microsoft, Alphabet, Goldman Sachs, Broadcom, Verizon, Wells Fargo, Arm Holdings and Intuit. The notice gives no reason for any objection and no launch date.

Get Unchained's crypto news in your inbox with the free Unchained Daily newsletter.

How an Objection Works

The SEC's tokenized securities venue exemption, an order dated Sept. 17 that is set to expire Sept. 17, 2031, lets an issuer keep its stock off such a venue. When a third party unaffiliated with the company makes the token, the venue must notify the issuer and wait at least 30 calendar days before trading starts. If an issuer objects in writing during that window, the token can't trade. The venue gets five business days after that to list the objection in an updated notice.

The venue is operated by OKXICE LLC, a Texas company owned 50% by ICE and 50% by OKC USA Holding, the joint venture the two firms formed. Trading will run through permissioned Uniswap v4 pools on XLayer, which will be open only to wallets holding a soulbound token (SBT) that OKXICE issues. The notice states the venue is not registered with the SEC for these activities and "is not subject to Regulation NMS."

Risks the Venue Discloses

The notice repeats risk warnings that have appeared in earlier versions. Decrypt reported on Oct. 25, citing the Oct. 23 notice, that administrators could change the venue's contracts with no warning to users and that the contract controlling trading access had been reviewed only in-house.

"The SBT smart contract has been audited internally, but not by external auditors," the notice says in its risk section. A second contract, the hook that checks those tokens on every trade, is to be audited internally and by Certified Kernel Tech LLC before it goes live.

Administrator keys for the contracts are managed by OKX Technology Inc., and contract changes "take effect without a timelock, so TSV Participants may receive no advance notice of an upgrade," according to the notice.

On investor protection, the venue writes that whether tokens "held in a self-custodied wallet would be treated as customer property or protected by the Securities Investor Protection Corporation is uncertain, and any recovery could be delayed or incomplete."

A $10,000 investment in NetApp (NTAP) stock grew to $65,318 over the past ten years before dividends. The same capital in the S&P 500 reached $35,820. In hindsight, deciding to buy looks like the only question, but the harder test was holding on. How many times do you think NetApp stock fell 20% or more on the way up?

How Often Did NetApp Stock Fall?

Over the past ten years, NetApp stock fell 20% or more three times, with each decline ultimately exceeding 30%.

The deepest drop stretched from September 2018 to March 2020, a period when the stock lost 59.8% and the S&P 500 fell 22.8%. Shareholders then waited another 17.2 months after that low until August 2021 before NetApp again closed above its September 2018 high.

What Did Holding NetApp Through A Fall Feel Like?

The most recent downturn began in July 2024 and lasted 8.8 months. At the April 2025 low, the position was down 43.5%. The stock then took another 13.6 months, until May 2026, to finally close above its July 2024 high.

Every one of NetApp's declines eventually ended. Yet an investor holding shares at the April 2025 low had no way to know that this drop would reverse, or when.

Was Something Wrong With NetApp's Business?

NetApp's twelve-month revenue fell during only one of the three stock declines, which was the deepest. The company sells data storage primarily through its Hybrid Cloud business, a segment accounting for 90.1% of revenue in fiscal 2026. The rest came from Public Cloud, encompassing storage services sold in the public cloud.

During that deepest drop, twelve-month revenue was 7.7% lower at the March 2020 low than at the September 2018 high. The operating margin barely shifted over the same period, edging from 17.7% to 17.2%. The business weakened only slightly, yet the stock dropped far more than revenue did.

The 2024 downturn unfolded differently. Twelve-month revenue at the April 2025 low was 3.8% higher than at the July 2024 high, and the operating margin climbed from 20.2% to 21.5%. The business remained solid by both measures, so the 43.5% drop did not come from weaker revenue or margins.

What Selling NetApp Stock Would Have Cost

NetApp stock has gained 528.2% since its March 2020 low, and anyone who sold at the bottom missed the entire rally. Today, the shares trade 7.1% below the highest close of the ten years, which occurred on October 12, 2026.
